Missing: any SandboxBackend seam (the 2026-08-22 ledger entry declined it until a second backend is planned), a microVM or remote backend, thread-scoped lease and workspace for non-Space chats, idle-stop and snapshot-to-object-storage VM lifecycle, typed failure causes and heartbeat, VM-seconds metering and any lifecycle UI; the inline ExecuteStep chat path still loses workspace edits.

constraints: Decision ledger 2026-08-22 rejects a SandboxBackend trait until a second real backend is planned, so an ADR must reverse that first. sandbox-manager owns rows and authority but not execution; the OS process lives in execution-core, and backend identity is today a per-instance env (SANDBOX_MANAGER_BACKEND_ID) that Control's decision pins. Space access never widens: a thread-scoped workspace for non-Space turns needs its own Control-signed decision and must not alias Space workspaces. ZDR runs must stay ephemeral (no snapshot, no content in logs). approachAdjustment: The seam is in the wrong service: put the backend abstraction on execution-core's spawn/execute contract (Rust trait with bwrap and a remote-executor client), keep sandbox-manager as lease/registry authority and extend it with typed lifecycle, failure-cause and heartbeat fields. A microVM can first land as a second attested executor plus sandbox-manager pair with its own backend_id and a profile that says persistence durable, using the existing Control decision as the gate. Smallest first slice: thread-scoped lease and workspace on bwrap, which also fixes the inline-ExecuteStep edit loss. Write the ADR that reverses the 2026-08-22 deferral before phase 2.
effortNote: Unchanged overall; phase 1 (seam, thread workspace on bwrap, typed lifecycle) is about M, the microVM backend with snapshots and metering is the XL.
verdictReason: Status is correctly partial, but the item places the trait in sandbox-manager (a bookkeeping service) and ignores the standing ledger decision and the existing Control-signed backend pin; the build should be ADR-first with the seam in execution-core.

Memory already has lineage (supersedes_id, is_latest, review_state) that a ledger can project.

constraints: ZDR and waived runs must stay excluded (already enforced twice; keep). Owner scoping collides with the gateway skill cache: MatchSkills and fetch_skill_context pull ListAgentSkills once per org per TTL with the triggering caller's bearer, session-core filters that list by caller, and replace_learned prunes anything not in the pull, so user-scoped learned skills would flap or be missing for their owner unless the cache is pulled with a service-wide view (visibility stays per-caller in OwnershipStore) or keyed per user (INF from reading both paths). Skills only support scope org|user (CHECK constraint), so learning from a shared-Space thread has no Space scope to land in; exclude Space-audience runs or hold them as proposals. PromoteSkill was removed (SKILL-2) because Capability.Scope had no authorization effect; org promotion must go through the admin-only org-skill creation path, not a revived workflow. The review model call uses a service credential (owner decision OD4 is open).
approachAdjustment: Do the cheap safe fix first: pass env.UserID through SessionRef, add scope, owner_user_id and a disabled-by-default or status field to UpsertAgentSkillRequest, write learned skills as user-scoped proposals, stop the upsert from re-enabling an admin-disabled row, and return origin from the capability-core list. Fix the gateway skill cache for per-user visibility before relying on owner scope. Then the inbox and org promotion as 'admin copies a proposal into an org skill', then the seeded eval and a skill_revisions table; do not revive SkillPromotionWorkflow.
effortNote: Unchanged; the staging-gate slice (owner scope, disabled by default, origin in list, cache fix) is about M and should ship first.
verdictReason: The governance gap is real and directly confirmed in code (org-wide default scope, no status, no inbox, no eval); the approach needs the owner-scope plumbing and gateway cache constraint added, but the item stands.

verdictReason: The built-not-deployed fix is now in the repo and its deployment is an ops task whose state cannot be proven from code; the new build (chain, verifier, compliance API, SIEM) is genuinely absent but must account for retention purge and multi-producer ordering.

constraints: No cross-plane DB: the full-text index must live in session-core (Model Plane Postgres), not in Data Plane v2 whose tsvector migration is documents only. ZDR turns must be excluded from the index and indexed rows must honour the durable erase contract on thread delete (http_routes.rs); Space-audience threads (migration 0025) need a Control-signed Space read decision for search and recall and must never widen an owner ACL. The rejected-design failure modes recorded in CHAT_RESUME_AND_VERSIONS_SPEC must be designed out: context assembly, learning review (ListConversation), Dreaming memory extraction, compaction and audit must read the active path only, effectful turns stay immutable, and branch semantics (OD19) are unresolved. recall results are a prompt-injection channel and stay owner-scoped.

verdictReason: Gaps are real (no tree, search, recall, paging) but the item understates that persisted versions were explicitly rejected once and that server-side pin and archive already exist; the tree must be sequenced after the independent search and paging work.

constraints: Web tools execute in two places: model-gateway's inline loop (quarry.rs, tools.rs) and execution-core's web_tools.rs for agent runs, and the source-scope prune exists only in the former, so an org policy must be enforced in both and re-validated by Quarry (Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects). Quarry can only re-check what reaches it in a form it can trust, so the policy needs a signed or Control-fetched path, and a long domain list in a bearer claim is a poor fit. ZDR must propagate: the zdr flag already reaches the edge, and cached-only mode must not add a new egress. Policy authority is Control Plane (org-core); enforcement is Model Plane plus Quarry, so 'planeOwner: Control Plane' alone is wrong.
approachAdjustment: Store the policy in org-core and read it through a narrow service endpoint with fail-closed caching like the retention posture, rather than minting domain lists into the capability bearer; pass a policy revision to Quarry on every call and let Quarry enforce. Enforce in both gateway and execution-core paths. Ship the separable, small part first: have Quarry return provider and reason, forward them in tool_result and grounding events, and render 'Searched via X' in the Sources panel. Verify the provider table against smart_router.rs and the serp module before publishing it: the router struct holds tantivy, stract, SearXNG, Brave and Serper while gateway doc comments name tavily, bing and google.
effortNote: Raised from M: policy record plus admin UI, enforcement in two loops, a new Quarry cached-only mode and signed policy path, and the consent card; the 'Searched via' slice alone is S to M.
verdictReason: Gaps are real and nothing equivalent exists, but the item mis-assigns ownership (Control Plane only), omits the execution-core web path, and proposes a bearer-claim carrier that the org-core retention-posture precedent argues against.
